## Final Accepted Amendments

### `fr-7-f0d55cc5`

In `enforce_invariants` (invariants.rs), the function applies clamping mutations (pH, indices, DO) to `&mut TankState` before reaching later validation checks (`check_unit_interval`, `check_sum_close_to_one`, `check_non_negative` for reserve_g). If a later check returns `Err`, the state has already been partially mutated by earlier clamps. The new tests in validation.rs (lines 92-127) assert `engine.full_state() == &expected` after an error, which only holds because `TankState::new()` currently produces a state where all clamp operations are no-ops. Fix: either (a) move all pure validation checks before any clamping mutations so errors are returned on unmodified state, or (b) remove the post-error state-equality assertions from tests since they encode a fragile assumption.

### `fr-7-6c8fdcb3`

crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:230-235,443-446,530-533,626-656 and crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:85-91: the new hatching/maturation funding path pulls biomass from dissolved water pools even though feeding explicitly routes the retained share into animal.reserve_g and documents that reserve as the store used for growth/reproduction. reserve_g is never debited, so retained mass becomes a dead-end pool while successful hatches/maturation depend on DON/TAN/DOC/DIC instead of stored food. This is already visible in crates/tank_core/tests/shrimp_population.rs:103-117: cargo test -p tank_core --test shrimp_population hatch_produces_juveniles now fails under the "good conditions" fixture. Hatching and juvenile maturation should spend reserve_g (or reserve first, then water if that is the intended model) rather than bypassing it.

### `fr-7-baf66be2`

crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:524-545 and 563-600: the tracked-budget guard is disabled wholesale whenever a tick contains any non-zero action:feed/action:water_change/action:siphon_detritus/action:add_shrimp/action:remove_shrimp flux. That means a tick with a legitimate open-system action and an unrelated leak later in the hour will never raise BudgetImbalance; the action delta masks the rest of the tick instead of being subtracted from the residual. You already do the right residual-based subtraction for chemistry carbon at crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:577-589. Apply the same pattern to open-system action fluxes so mixed ticks still detect unexplained nitrogen/carbon drift.
